subtitle: Lesson 8 · Security Architecture Frameworks

code:
SABSA  -> business traceability
TOGAF  -> repeatable EA process
ZTMM   -> technology-domain maturity baseline

Committing to one, before understanding the org,
repeats SABSA's own warning: a control (or a
framework) not tied to a real requirement isn't
architecture.
caption: Three real frameworks, three different problems solved.

eyebrow: Questions that should drive the choice

steps.label: Does EA already exist?
steps.sub: Integrate into TOGAF rather than compete with it

steps.label: What's driving this?
steps.sub: Audit, incident, growth, or greenfield build

steps.label: How much governance fits?
steps.sub: A 30-person startup can't sustain a full ADM cycle

code:
TOGAF (outer process) + SABSA (inner content)
  -> ADM governs cadence; SABSA fills security content

ZTMM as a technology-domain input
  -> feeds Phase D / E / F, not a standalone framework

Lightweight SABSA subset
  -> just the Business Attributes Profile + traceability
caption: Most mature organizations blend rather than pick exactly one.

eyebrow: Adapt, don't implement by the book
code:
Rigid, full implementation on an org that doesn't
need it yet -> paperwork that drifts, ignored when
it matters most (audit, incident, board review)

Adapted to real size/maturity/driver
  -> artifacts people actually keep using
caption: The real skill: diagnosing which parts of which framework THIS org needs now.
